name: 〜to naru (〜となる) — to become / turn into (formal)

explanation.en:
〜to naru (〜となる) attaches to nouns or noun-equivalents. Means 'become / turn into X' — formal / written equivalent of 〜ni naru. The と here marks the end-state. otona to naru (<ruby>大人<rt>おとな</rt></ruby>となる) 'become an adult'. Conjugates: 〜to natta (past), 〜to naru darou (will probably become).

Distinguished from 〜ni naru (everyday spoken 'become') by register. 〜to naru is preferred in formal writing, news, business prose, song lyrics aiming for weight. The と implies a definite identification or conclusion: kekka to naru (<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>となる) 'becomes the result'.

Compare with 〜ni naru (everyday become), 〜ni kawaru (change into — batch5b), 〜da to naru (becomes the case that). 〜to naru is the elevated 'becomes' marker — perfect for transitions, conclusions, transformations in formal context.

• otona to naru (<ruby>大人<rt>おとな</rt></ruby>となる) — 'become an adult'
• kekka to naru (<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes the result'
• mokuteki to naru (<ruby>目的<rt>もくてき</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes the goal'
• shimei to naru (<ruby>使命<rt>しめい</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes (one's) mission'
• yume to naru (<ruby>夢<rt>ゆめ</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes a dream'
• kioku to naru (<ruby>記憶<rt>きおく</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes a memory'
• inori to naru (<ruby>祈<rt>いの</rt></ruby>りとなる) — 'becomes a prayer'
• namida to naru (<ruby>涙<rt>なみだ</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes tears'
• unmei to naru (<ruby>運命<rt>うんめい</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes fate'
• ai to naru (<ruby>愛<rt>あい</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes love'
• kotoba to naru (<ruby>言葉<rt>ことば</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes words'
• kanashimi to naru (<ruby>悲<rt>かな</rt></ruby>しみとなる) — 'becomes sadness'
• boku no chikara to naru (<ruby>僕<rt>ぼく</rt></ruby>の<ruby>力<rt>ちから</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes my strength'
• hikari to naru (<ruby>光<rt>ひかり</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes light'
• boku-tachi no kioku to naru (<ruby>僕<rt>ぼく</rt></ruby>たちの<ruby>記憶<rt>きおく</rt></ruby>となる) — 'becomes our memory'

name: 〜to shite (〜として) — as / in the capacity of

explanation.en:
〜to shite (〜として) attaches to nouns. Means 'as / in the capacity of X / treating as X'. Marks a role or perspective: gakusei to shite (<ruby>学生<rt>がくせい</rt></ruby>として) 'as a student'. shujinkou to shite (<ruby>主人公<rt>しゅじんこう</rt></ruby>として) 'as the protagonist'. Defines the speaker's standpoint or the role of the subject.

Used in formal speech, professional contexts, and abstract perspective-taking. Often paired with hito, hitori, mono: hitori to shite (<ruby>一人<rt>ひとり</rt></ruby>として) 'as an individual'. Combined with 〜mo + negative produces 'not even one X' — hitori to shite inai (<ruby>一人<rt>ひとり</rt></ruby>として いない) 'not a single person is here'.

Compare with 〜da kara (because — reason), 〜tame ni (in order to / for the sake of, batch2 — purpose), 〜to shite mo (even supposing, batch3b — concession). 〜to shite is the role / capacity marker — 'in the role of X, the action proceeds'.

• gakusei to shite (<ruby>学生<rt>がくせい</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a student'
• otona to shite (<ruby>大人<rt>おとな</rt></ruby>として) — 'as an adult'
• tomodachi to shite (<ruby>友達<rt>ともだち</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a friend'
• kazoku to shite (<ruby>家族<rt>かぞく</rt></ruby>として) — 'as family'
• hitori to shite (<ruby>一人<rt>ひとり</rt></ruby>として) — 'as an individual'
• boku to shite wa (<ruby>僕<rt>ぼく</rt></ruby>としては) — 'as for me / from my perspective'
• kekka to shite (<ruby>結果<rt>けっか</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a result'
• koibito to shite (<ruby>恋人<rt>こいびと</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a lover'
• ningen to shite (<ruby>人間<rt>にんげん</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a human being'
• shujinkou to shite (<ruby>主人公<rt>しゅじんこう</rt></ruby>として) — 'as the protagonist'
• riyuu to shite (<ruby>理由<rt>りゆう</rt></ruby>として) — 'as a reason'
• shouko to shite (<ruby>証拠<rt>しょうこ</rt></ruby>として) — 'as evidence'
• hitori to shite mo wakaranai (<ruby>一人<rt>ひとり</rt></ruby>としても<ruby>分<rt>わ</rt></ruby>からない) — 'not a single person understands'
• boku no kotoba to shite (<ruby>僕<rt>ぼく</rt></ruby>の<ruby>言葉<rt>ことば</rt></ruby>として) — 'as my words'
• kioku to shite nokoru (<ruby>記憶<rt>きおく</rt></ruby>として<ruby>残<rt>のこ</rt></ruby>る) — 'remain as a memory'

name: 〜toka 〜toka (〜とか〜とか) — things like X and Y (casual listing)

explanation.en:
〜toka 〜toka (〜とか〜とか) is a casual listing construction. Attaches to nouns or V-dictionary forms. Means 'things like X and Y / X, Y, and so on'. Less formal than 〜nado, more casual than 〜tari 〜tari. Very common in spoken Japanese for non-exhaustive examples. ramen toka sushi toka (ラーメンとか<ruby>寿司<rt>すし</rt></ruby>とか) 'things like ramen and sushi'.

Often used for hedged descriptions or vague enumerations: gakkou de benkyou toka asobi toka (<ruby>学校<rt>がっこう</rt></ruby>で<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>遊<rt>あそ</rt></ruby>びとか) 'studying and playing and stuff at school'. Sometimes a single 〜toka appears alone with implied 'etc.': eiga toka mireba ii (<ruby>映画<rt>えいが</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ればいい) 'maybe watch a movie or something'.

Compare with 〜tari 〜tari (verbs only, batch3a), 〜nado (formal etc), 〜ya (formal listing). 〜toka 〜toka is the everyday casual listing — friendly, hedged, exemplary. In songs and conversation, signals 'these examples and similar'.

• ramen toka sushi toka (ラーメンとか<ruby>寿司<rt>すし</rt></ruby>とか) — 'things like ramen and sushi'
• benkyou toka asobi toka (<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>遊<rt>あそ</rt></ruby>びとか) — 'studying and playing'
• warau toka naku toka (<ruby>笑<rt>わら</rt></ruby>うとか<ruby>泣<rt>な</rt></ruby>くとか) — 'laughing and crying and such'
• ai toka yume toka (<ruby>愛<rt>あい</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>夢<rt>ゆめ</rt></ruby>とか) — 'love and dreams and so on'
• kanji toka hiragana toka (<ruby>漢字<rt>かんじ</rt></ruby>とかひらがなとか) — 'kanji and hiragana and so on'
• shippai toka seikou toka (<ruby>失敗<rt>しっぱい</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>成功<rt>せいこう</rt></ruby>とか) — 'failure and success and such'
• kazoku toka tomodachi toka (<ruby>家族<rt>かぞく</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>友達<rt>ともだち</rt></ruby>とか) — 'family and friends and so on'
• eiga toka mireba ii (<ruby>映画<rt>えいが</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>見<rt>み</rt></ruby>ればいい) — 'maybe watch a movie or something'
• haru toka aki toka (<ruby>春<rt>はる</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>秋<rt>あき</rt></ruby>とか) — 'spring and autumn and so on'
• boku toka kimi toka (<ruby>僕<rt>ぼく</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>君<rt>きみ</rt></ruby>とか) — 'people like me and you'
• tsukareta toka kanashii toka (<ruby>疲<rt>つか</rt></ruby>れたとか<ruby>悲<rt>かな</rt></ruby>しいとか) — 'tired and sad and stuff'
• namida toka warai toka (<ruby>涙<rt>なみだ</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>笑<rt>わら</rt></ruby>いとか) — 'tears and laughter and so on'
• yorokobi toka kanashimi toka (<ruby>喜<rt>よろこ</rt></ruby>びとか<ruby>悲<rt>かな</rt></ruby>しみとか) — 'joy and sorrow and such'
• mukashi toka ima toka (<ruby>昔<rt>むかし</rt></ruby>とか<ruby>今<rt>いま</rt></ruby>とか) — 'past and present and so on'
• kotae toka shitsumon toka (<ruby>答<rt>こた</rt></ruby>えとか<ruby>質問<rt>しつもん</rt></ruby>とか) — 'answers and questions and so on'

name: 〜tto (〜っと) — onomatopoeic / quick-action emphasis

explanation.en:
〜tto (〜っと) is an onomatopoeic / quick-action emphasis particle. Attaches to verbs (often imperative or volitional), adjectives, or appears at the end of action descriptions. Marks decisive, sudden, or punctuated action. yotto (よっと) — interjection 'oof / there!' on completing an action. mippai-tto (ぐいっと) — 'in one gulp'.

Often attached to manner adverbs (gui, suk, sak, pita, etc.) to form mimetic compounds: pita-tto tomatta (ピタッと<ruby>止<rt>と</rt></ruby>まった) 'stopped sharply'. The 〜tto adds crispness / definitiveness to the action description, almost a sound effect rendered as text.

Compare with bare adverb (without っと, less crisp), 〜to (formal quotative — different role), 〜tte (casual quotative, batch4a). 〜tto is the snap-emphasis marker — common in songs for vivid action imagery and in spoken language for punctuating descriptions.

• gui-tto nomu (グイッと<ruby>飲<rt>の</rt></ruby>む) — 'drink in one gulp'
• pita-tto tomaru (ピタッと<ruby>止<rt>と</rt></ruby>まる) — 'stop sharply'
• suk-tto kokoro ga hareru (スッと<ruby>心<rt>こころ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>晴<rt>は</rt></ruby>れる) — 'heart clears suddenly'
• yotto (よっと) — 'oof / there!'
• kotto (コトッと) — 'with a small clink'
• don-tto okita (ドンッと<ruby>起<rt>お</rt></ruby>きた) — 'jumped up with a thud'
• gyu-tto dakishimeru (ギュッと<ruby>抱<rt>だ</rt></ruby>きしめる) — 'hug tightly'
• pyo-tto deru (ピョッと<ruby>出<rt>で</rt></ruby>る) — 'pop out'
• fu-tto warau (フッと<ruby>笑<rt>わら</rt></ruby>う) — 'chuckle softly'
• cha-tto suru (チャッとする) — 'do it quickly'
• kira-tto kagayaku (キラッと<ruby>輝<rt>かがや</rt></ruby>く) — 'sparkle'
• puchi-tto kireru (プチッと<ruby>切<rt>き</rt></ruby>れる) — 'snap (lose patience)'
• doki-tto suru (ドキッとする) — 'startle / heart skips'
• biku-tto suru (ビクッとする) — 'flinch'
• sat-tto kawaru (サッと<ruby>変<rt>か</rt></ruby>わる) — 'change in a flash'

<!-- v2-romaji-primary -->

name: 〜てくぜ (gonna do it - masculine)

explanation.en:
How it works: Combine the て-form + いく (iku, 'to go') + ぜ (ze, masculine emphasis particle). This creates an energetic, masculine declaration — 'I'm gonna keep doing it!' The いく often contracts away.

Example from this song: The song uses this pattern to express determined forward momentum with a rough, energetic masculine tone.

More examples:
• 行く (iku, 'to go') → 行ってくぜ (ittekuze, 'I'm heading out!')
• やる (yaru, 'to do') → やってくぜ (yattekuze, 'I'm gonna do it!')
• 走る (hashiru, 'to run') → 走ってくぜ (hashittekuze, 'I'm gonna run!')

Note: ぜ (ze) is a rough masculine sentence-ending particle that adds energy and assertion. It's less aggressive than ぞ (zo). Common in shonen anime and J-rock. Think Naruto saying 行くってばよ (ikuttebayo) — similarly energetic but different particle.

name: 〜なかった (nakatta - could not / did not)

explanation.en:
The past negative form of verbs, meaning "could not" or "did not." One of the most fundamental conjugations in Japanese.

How it works:
Take the ない-form (nai-form) of a verb, replace ない (nai) with なかった (nakatta).

Example from this song:
果たせなかった約束 (hatasenakatta yakusoku, "Promises we could not fulfill")

More examples:
- 行けなかった (ikenakatta, "could not go")
- 食べなかった (tabenakatta, "did not eat")
- 間に合わなかった (ma ni awanakatta, "did not make it in time")

name: 〜のか (rhetorical question)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add のか (no ka) at the end of a sentence to create an emotionally charged question, often rhetorical. の adds an explanatory tone, and か marks the question. Together they express doubt, frustration, or deep wondering.

Example from this song: The song uses のか to question reality with emotional weight — 'Is it really...?' or 'Can it be that...?'

More examples:
• 何 (nani, 'what') → 何なのか (nan na no ka, 'what is it, really?')
• できる (dekiru, 'can do') → できるのか (dekiru no ka, 'can it really be done?')
• 本当 (hontō, 'true') → 本当なのか (hontō na no ka, 'is it really true?')

Note: In casual male speech, のか often drops to のか without rising intonation, making it sound reflective rather than questioning. It adds more emotional weight than plain か alone.

name: 〜のかな (no kana) — I wonder if

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb/Adjective plain form + のかな (no kana) expresses casual wondering — "I wonder if ~." The の (no) adds explanatory nuance, and かな (kana) expresses uncertainty or self-directed questioning. It is softer and more reflective than a direct question. Very common in song lyrics and inner monologue.

Example from this song:
今もあるのかな (ima mo aru no kana) — "I wonder if it's still there"
The singer gently wonders whether something from the past still exists.

More examples:
• 元気にしてるのかな (genki ni shiteru no kana) — "I wonder if they're doing well"
• これで良かったのかな (kore de yokatta no kana) — "I wonder if this was the right thing"
• 覚えてるのかな (oboeteru no kana) — "I wonder if they remember"

name: 〜のせい (because of; due to)

explanation.en:
How it works: のせい (no sei) means 'because of' or 'due to,' specifically when attributing blame or a negative cause. It implies the cause is at fault.

Example from this song: The song uses のせい to blame something for a negative outcome — 'it's because of (something bad).'

More examples:
• 雨のせいで遅れた (ame no sei de okureta, 'was late because of the rain') — from 雨 (ame, 'rain')
• 君のせいだ (kimi no sei da, 'it's your fault') — from 君 (kimi, 'you')
• 寝不足のせいで (nebusoku no sei de, 'because of lack of sleep')

Note: のせい is for negative causes (blame). For positive causes, use おかげで (okage de, 'thanks to'). 君のせいで泣いた (your fault I cried) vs. 君のおかげで笑えた (thanks to you I could smile).

name: 〜のままに (no mama ni: as it is; following)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + のままに (no mama ni) to express following something without resistance — 'as X dictates' or 'following the flow of X'. まま means 'as is' and に indicates manner.

Example from this song: 衝動のままに (shoudou no mama ni) = 'following the impulse / as the impulse dictates' — from 衝動 (shoudou, 'impulse') + の (no) + ままに (mama ni, 'as is')

More examples:
• 心 (kokoro, 'heart') → 心のままに (kokoro no mama ni, 'following your heart')
• 気持ち (kimochi, 'feeling') → 気持ちのままに (kimochi no mama ni, 'as your feelings dictate')
• 流れ (nagare, 'flow') → 流れのままに (nagare no mama ni, 'going with the flow')

Note: ままに implies surrendering control and letting something guide you. Without に, まま means the state remains unchanged: そのまま (sono mama, 'as it is').

name: 〜の方が (no hou ga: the ... one is more)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use A の方が (no hou ga) + adjective to express that A has MORE of that quality. It's the comparison pattern — 'A is more [adj] (than B)'.

Example from this song: 嘘の方がずっと痛かった (uso no hou ga zutto itakatta) = 'the lie was far more painful' — from 嘘 (uso, 'lie') + の方が (no hou ga, 'is more') + ずっと (zutto, 'far more') + 痛かった (itakatta, 'was painful')

More examples:
• こっち (kocchi, 'this one') → こっちの方がいい (kocchi no hou ga ii, 'this one is better')
• 歩く (aruku, 'to walk') → 歩いた方がいい (aruita hou ga ii, 'it's better to walk')
• 夏 (natsu, 'summer') → 夏の方が好き (natsu no hou ga suki, 'I like summer more')

Note: For nouns: A の方が. For verbs (advice): た-form + 方がいい = 'you should'. ずっと (zutto, 'much more') intensifies the comparison. This song's line powerfully says lies hurt MORE than the truth.

name: 〜はしない (emphatic negation)

explanation.en: Verb stem + は + しない is a strong, often defiant negation: 'won't (do that), no way'. かないはしない 'no enemy can stand a chance'; 捨てはしない 'I won't throw it away'. Stronger than plain 〜ない.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + は + しない es negación enfática, a menudo desafiante. かないはしない 'ningún enemigo está a la altura'; 捨てはしない 'no lo voy a tirar'. Más fuerte que 〜ない.
explanation.pt-BR: Radical do verbo + は + しない é negação enfática, frequentemente desafiadora. かないはしない 'nenhum inimigo é páreo'; 捨てはしない 'não vou jogar fora'. Mais forte que 〜ない.

name: 〜はじめる (begin to)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the verb masu-stem and add はじめる (hajimeru, 'to begin'). This creates a compound verb meaning 'to begin doing something'.

Example from this song: つかみはじめた (tsukami hajimeta) = 'began to grasp' — from つかむ (tsukamu, 'to grasp') → つかみ (tsukami, masu-stem) + はじめた (hajimeta, past of hajimeru)

More examples:
• 降る (furu, 'to fall') → 降りはじめる (furi hajimeru, 'begin to fall — rain starting')
• 読む (yomu, 'to read') → 読みはじめる (yomi hajimeru, 'begin to read')
• 分かる (wakaru, 'to understand') → 分かりはじめる (wakari hajimeru, 'begin to understand')

Note: Compare with 〜だす (dasu), which also means 'begin to' but implies a more sudden or unexpected start. はじめる is a gradual, intentional beginning.

name: 〜べき (beki: should)

explanation.en:
How it works: べき (beki) attaches to the dictionary form of a verb to express 'should' or 'ought to.' It indicates a moral obligation or something that is expected.

Example from this song: 愛されるべき (aisareru beki) = 'should be loved' — from 愛される (aisareru, 'to be loved', passive of 愛する) + べき (beki)

More examples:
• 行くべきだ (iku beki da, 'should go') — from 行く (iku, 'to go')
• 知るべきことだ (shiru beki koto da, 'something you should know') — from 知る (shiru, 'to know')
• やるべきことをやる (yaru beki koto o yaru, 'do what should be done') — from やる (yaru, 'to do')

Note: べき is stronger than ほうがいい (hou ga ii, 'it would be better'). The exception is する → するべき or すべき (both are correct). べき implies duty or moral correctness.

name: 〜ますように (may it be that... — wish form)

explanation.en: Verb + ますように expresses a wish: 雨が湿らせますように = 'may the rain dampen it'; 合格しますように ('may I pass'); 元気でいますように ('may you stay well'). Standard wording on tanabata strips and prayer plaques (絵馬).
explanation.es: Verbo + ますように expresa un deseo: 雨が湿らせますように, 合格しますように, 元気でいますように. Forma estándar en tiras del tanabata y ema (tablillas votivas).
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo + ますように exprime um desejo: 雨が湿らせますように, 合格しますように, 元気でいますように. Frase padrão em tiras do tanabata e ema (placas de oração).

name: 〜まみれ (covered in, smeared with)

explanation.en: Noun + まみれ means 'covered in / drenched in'. Like だらけ but specifically for sticky/wet things — blood, mud, sweat, oil. Aqua Timez extends it to abstract nouns: 挫折まみれ 'covered in setbacks'.
explanation.es: Sustantivo + まみれ significa 'cubierto de / empapado en'. Similar a だらけ, pero para cosas pegajosas/húmedas. 挫折まみれ 'cubierto de fracasos'.
explanation.pt-BR: Substantivo + まみれ significa 'coberto de / banhado em'. Parecido com だらけ mas mais para líquidos/grude. 挫折まみれ 'coberto de fracassos'.

name: 〜まるで...のように (marude... no you ni: just like)

explanation.en:
How it works: まるで (marude) means 'just like' and pairs with のように (no you ni) or みたいに (mitai ni) to create vivid similes. It emphasizes how closely something resembles something else.

Example from this song: まるで人生だから (marude jinsei dakara) = 'because it's just like life' — comparing the situation to life itself, from 人生 (jinsei, 'life')

More examples:
• まるで映画のように (marude eiga no you ni, 'just like a movie') — from 映画 (eiga, 'movie')
• まるで夢のようだ (marude yume no you da, 'it's just like a dream') — from 夢 (yume, 'dream')
• まるで別人のように変わった (marude betsujin no you ni kawatta, 'changed as if a different person')

Note: まるで adds emphasis to the comparison. Without まるで, のように still works but sounds less dramatic. みたいに is the casual equivalent of のように.

name: 〜も〜も (mo ... mo) — both ... and ...

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern X + も (mo) + Y + も (mo) means "both X and Y" or "X as well as Y." It emphasizes that multiple things share the same quality or are included equally. It can also be used with negatives to mean "neither X nor Y" when followed by a negative verb.

Example from this song:
The singer lists multiple things that are equally important or equally lost, using も...も to give them equal weight.

More examples:
• 日本語も英語も話せる (nihongo mo eigo mo hanaseru) — "can speak both Japanese and English"
• 時間もお金もない (jikan mo okane mo nai) — "have neither time nor money"
• 父も母も元気です (chichi mo haha mo genki desu) — "both my father and mother are well"

name: 〜ゆく (yuku - literary 〜ていく)

explanation.en:
A literary/poetic form of 〜ていく (te iku), expressing a gradual change moving away from the speaker. Common in poetry and song lyrics.

How it works:
Attach ゆく (yuku) to the masu-stem of a verb. It replaces the more casual ていく (te iku).

Example from this song:
奪われゆく生命 (ubarare yuku seimei, "Lives being gradually taken away")

More examples:
- 消えゆく光 (kie yuku hikari, "Light fading away")
- 過ぎゆく時 (sugi yuku toki, "Time passing by")
- 変わりゆく世界 (kawari yuku sekai, "A world that is changing")

name: 〜ようにする (yō ni suru — as if doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ように (yō ni) after a verb in dictionary form to express manner — 'as if doing X' or 'in such a way that X'. It can describe how an action is performed.

Example from this song: 言い聞かせるように (iikikaseru yō ni) = 'as if telling oneself' — from 言い聞かせる (iikikaseru, 'to tell oneself') + ように (yō ni, 'as if')

More examples:
• 歌う (utau, 'to sing') → 歌うように (utau yō ni, 'as if singing')
• 飛ぶ (tobu, 'to fly') → 飛ぶように (tobu yō ni, 'as if flying')
• 祈る (inoru, 'to pray') → 祈るように (inoru yō ni, 'as if praying')

Note: ように has multiple uses. With する it means 'try to / make sure to': 忘れないようにする (wasurenai yō ni suru, 'make sure not to forget'). Without する, it describes manner.

name: 〜を超えて (to surpass; beyond)

explanation.en:
How it works: を超えて (o koete) means 'going beyond' or 'surpassing.' 超える (koeru) means 'to exceed,' and in te-form it connects to the next action or description.

Example from this song: 限界を超えて (genkai o koete) = 'surpassing the limits' — from 限界 (genkai, 'limit') + を (o) + 超えて (koete, 'exceeding')

More examples:
• 国境を超えて (kokkyou o koete, 'crossing borders') — from 国境 (kokkyou, 'national border')
• 想像を超えた (souzou o koeta, 'exceeded imagination') — from 想像 (souzou, 'imagination')
• 時を超えて (toki o koete, 'transcending time') — from 時 (toki, 'time')

Note: 超える (koeru) is a versatile verb. を超えて in te-form often connects to what happens after surpassing: 限界を超えて飛び出そう (genkai o koete tobidasou, 'let's break past our limits and leap out').

name: 〜を追い越す (o oikosu - to overtake)

explanation.en:
A compound verb meaning "to overtake" or "to pass by." Combines 追い (oi, "chase") + 越す (kosu, "cross over").

How it works:
Use を (o) to mark the object being overtaken, then 追い越す (oikosu).

Example from this song:
風を追い越して (kaze o oikoshite, "Overtaking the wind")

More examples:
- 車を追い越す (kuruma o oikosu, "to overtake a car")
- 時代を追い越す (jidai o oikosu, "to surpass the era")
- 先輩を追い越した (senpai o oikoshita, "surpassed my senior")

name: 〜んじゃないの (n ja nai no) — isn't it that / could it be

explanation.en:
How it works:
The pattern Verb/Adjective plain form + んじゃないの (n ja nai no) is a casual way to suggest or gently accuse — "isn't it that ~?" or "could it be ~?" It wraps a statement into a soft question or challenge. It can be confrontational or genuinely questioning, depending on tone.

Example from this song:
怖いんじゃないの (kowai n ja nai no) — "aren't you actually scared?"
The singer challenges someone, suggesting they are hiding their fear.

More examples:
• 本当は知ってるんじゃないの (hontou wa shitteru n ja nai no) — "don't you actually know?"
• 好きなんじゃないの (suki nan ja nai no) — "isn't it that you like them?"
• 嫌なんじゃないの (iya nan ja nai no) — "don't you actually dislike it?"

name: 〜ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai - cannot do)

explanation.en:
Expresses that something "cannot be done" due to social, moral, or situational reasons. It is stronger than できない (dekinai, "cannot") because it implies the speaker feels a moral or social obligation not to do something.

How it works:
Attach ワケにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai) after the dictionary form of a verb. The verb describes the action that is unacceptable.

Example from this song:
誰にも邪魔させるワケにはいかないから (dare ni mo jama saseru wake ni wa ikanai kara, "Because I cannot allow anyone to get in the way")

More examples:
- ここで諦めるワケにはいかない (koko de akirameru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot give up here")
- 嘘をつくワケにはいかない (uso o tsuku wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot tell a lie")
- 友達を裏切るワケにはいかない (tomodachi o uragiru wake ni wa ikanai, "I cannot betray my friend")

name: 〜前に (mae ni - before)

explanation.en:
Japanese equivalent of "before" as in "before you idealize." It marks a point in time before an action.

How it works:
Place 前に (mae ni) after the dictionary form of a verb.

Example from this song:
"Cultivate your hunger before you idealize" → 理想化する前に (risou-ka suru mae ni, "before you idealize")

More examples:
- 寝る前に歯を磨く (neru mae ni ha o migaku, "Brush your teeth before sleeping")
- 出かける前に確認する (dekakeru mae ni kakunin suru, "Check before going out")
- 食べる前に手を洗う (taberu mae ni te o arau, "Wash hands before eating")

name: 〜故に (yue ni - because of)

explanation.en:
A literary and formal way to say "because of" or "due to." It sounds much more elegant than the everyday から (kara) or ので (node). You will mostly find it in written Japanese, poetry, and song lyrics.

How it works:
Attach 故に (yue ni) after a verb in past tense, a noun, or a na-adjective + な. It marks the reason or cause for what follows.

Example from this song:
愛した故に芽生えた悪の花 (aishita yue ni mebaeta aku no hana, "Because I loved, a flower of evil bloomed")

More examples:
- 若さ故に (wakasa yue ni, "because of youth")
- 知らなかった故に (shiranakatta yue ni, "because I did not know")
- 彼女が好きだった故に (kanojo ga suki datta yue ni, "because I liked her")

name: せっかく〜のに/から (sekkaku: since the effort was made)

explanation.en:
How it works: Place せっかく (sekkaku) before a clause to emphasize that something special or effortful happened, and you should take advantage of it. Pairs with から (kara, 'so') or のに (noni, 'despite').

Example from this song: せっかく晴れたから (sekkaku hareta kara) = 'since it finally cleared up (don't waste it)' — from せっかく (sekkaku, 'with great effort/finally') + 晴れた (hareta, 'cleared up') + から (kara, 'so')

More examples:
• 来る (kuru, 'to come') → せっかく来たのに (sekkaku kita noni, 'you came all this way, and yet...')
• 作る (tsukuru, 'to make') → せっかく作ったから (sekkaku tsukutta kara, 'since I went to the trouble of making it')
• 休み (yasumi, 'holiday') → せっかくの休みだから (sekkaku no yasumi da kara, 'since it's a precious day off')

Note: せっかく + から = positive outcome ('since the effort was made, let's enjoy it'). せっかく + のに = wasted effort ('despite the effort, it was wasted'). With nouns: せっかくの + noun.

name: どうか (please / somehow)

explanation.en: Adverbial expression with two main senses: (1) 'please' (in pleading / praying) — どうか叶えて ('please make it come true'); (2) 'somehow' (in uncertainty) — どうか分からない ('somehow I don't know'). The pleading sense is most common, especially with imperatives or volitionals. More heartfelt than ください ('please give'). Smile for you's 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('heart, please race across the sky') is a prayer to the speaker's own heart.
explanation.es: Expresión adverbial con dos sentidos: (1) 'por favor' (suplicando / rezando) — どうか叶えて ('por favor haz que se cumpla'); (2) 'de alguna manera' (incertidumbre). El sentido de súplica es más común, especialmente con imperativos o volitivos. Más sentido que ください. El 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('corazón, por favor atraviesa el cielo') de Smile for you es una plegaria al propio corazón.
explanation.pt-BR: Expressão adverbial com dois sentidos: (1) 'por favor' (em súplica / oração) — どうか叶えて ('por favor faça realizar'); (2) 'algumamente' (em incerteza). O sentido de súplica é mais comum, especialmente com imperativos ou volitivos. Mais sentido que ください. O 心よ どうか遠く空を駆けて ('coração, por favor atravesse o céu') do Smile for you é uma prece ao próprio coração.

name: も particle (also/too, even)

explanation.en:
How it works: The particle も (mo) replaces は or が to mean 'also' or 'too'. When used with 今日 (kyou, 'today'), it implies 'today as well' — suggesting this is a repeated pleasant occurrence.

Example from this song:
• お日さまも笑ってる (ohisama mo waratteru) = 'even the sun is smiling' — も adds the sun to the list of those smiling, after みんな (everyone)
• 今日もいい天気 (kyou mo ii tenki) = 'today is also nice weather' — implies yesterday was nice too, and so is today

More examples:
• 私も行きます (watashi mo ikimasu, 'I'll go too')
• 猫も犬も好きです (neko mo inu mo suki desu, 'I like both cats and dogs')
• 明日も頑張ろう (ashita mo ganbarou, 'let's do our best tomorrow too')

Note: も replaces は and が, but stacks with other particles: にも, でも, からも.
explanation.es:
Cómo funciona: La partícula も (mo) reemplaza は o が para significar 'también'. Cuando se usa con 今日 (kyou, 'hoy'), implica 'hoy también' — sugiriendo que es una ocurrencia agradable repetida.

Ejemplo de la canción:
• お日さまも笑ってる = 'hasta el sol está sonriendo' — も agrega el sol a la lista de los que sonríen
• 今日もいい天気 = 'hoy también hace buen tiempo' — implica que ayer también hacía buen tiempo
explanation.pt-BR:
Como funciona: A partícula も (mo) substitui は ou が para significar 'também'. Quando usada com 今日 (kyou, 'hoje'), implica 'hoje também' — sugerindo que é uma ocorrência agradável repetida.

Exemplo da música:
• お日さまも笑ってる = 'até o sol está sorrindo' — も adiciona o sol à lista dos que sorriem
• 今日もいい天気 = 'hoje também está bom tempo' — implica que ontem também estava bom

name: 頂戴 (ちょうだい) please/give me

explanation.en:
How it works: ちょうだい (choudai) is a casual/feminine way to say 'please give me' or 'please do (for me).' It's softer and cuter than ください (kudasai).

Example from this song: The song uses ちょうだい as a soft, intimate request — 'give me' or 'please do.'

More examples:
• お水ちょうだい (omizu choudai, 'give me water, please') — from お水 (omizu, 'water')
• 見せてちょうだい (misete choudai, 'show me, please') — from 見せる (miseru, 'to show')
• もう少し待ってちょうだい (mou sukoshi matte choudai, 'please wait a bit more')

Note: ちょうだい comes from 頂戴 which originally means 'to humbly receive.' As a request form, it's casual and often used by women and children, or in intimate situations. Noun + ちょうだい = 'give me (noun).' Te-form + ちょうだい = 'please do (action).'

name: Absolute self-attribution 〜他の誰でもない / 〜以外の誰でもない

explanation.en: Pattern: noun + 他の (or 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'no one else but X.' Used for emphatic single-attribution: identifies a specific party as the absolute and only one responsible. 私 他の誰でもない = 'me — no one but me.' Compare 私だけ ('only me' — neutral): the 他の誰でもない version forces a contrast with all alternatives. Common in dramatic confessions and accusations.
explanation.es: Patrón: sustantivo + 他の (o 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'nadie más que X'. Usado para atribución única enfática: identifica a una parte específica como la única responsable. 私 他の誰でもない = 'yo — nadie más'. Compara con 私だけ ('solo yo' — neutro): la versión 他の誰でもない fuerza contraste con todas las alternativas. Común en confesiones y acusaciones dramáticas.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão: substantivo + 他の (ou 以外の) + 誰でもない = 'mais ninguém senão X'. Usado pra atribuição única enfática: identifica parte específica como única responsável. 私 他の誰でもない = 'eu — mais ninguém'. Compare com 私だけ ('só eu' — neutro): a versão 他の誰でもない força contraste com todas as alternativas. Comum em confissões e acusações dramáticas.

name: Adjective doubling for emphasis (深い深い, 青い青い)

explanation.en: Repeating an adjective intensifies it: 深い深い ('so very deep'), 青い青い ('a deep, vivid blue'), 長い長い ('long, long...'). Common in lyrics, fairy tales, and emotive prose. The repetition lengthens the syllabic feel and adds emotional weight rather than literal stacking.
explanation.es: Repetir el adjetivo lo intensifica: 深い深い ('muy profundo'), 青い青い ('un azul muy intenso'), 長い長い. Habitual en letras, cuentos y prosa emotiva. Aporta peso emocional, no suma literal.
explanation.pt-BR: Repetir o adjetivo intensifica: 深い深い ('muito profundo'), 青い青い ('um azul muito intenso'), 長い長い. Comum em letras, contos e prosa emotiva. Acrescenta peso emocional, não soma literal.

name: Adjective stem + がる (act as if / show as)

explanation.en: い-adjective stem + がる creates a verb meaning 'show / display X (outwardly)': 強がる ('act tough'), 痛がる ('show pain'), 嬉しがる ('show joy'), 寂しがる ('act lonely'). Used to describe how someone APPEARS, not what they actually feel. Often the appearance hides a different inner feeling.
explanation.es: Raíz de adjetivo い + がる forma verbo que significa 'mostrar / aparentar X': 強がる, 痛がる, 嬉しがる, 寂しがる. Describe cómo APARENTA estar otra persona, no lo que siente.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz de adjetivo い + がる cria verbo que significa 'demonstrar X / fingir X': 強がる, 痛がる, 嬉しがる, 寂しがる. Para descrever como ALGUÉM aparenta, não o que sente.

name: Adjective-stem + も + ない (negative emphasis)

explanation.en: Inserting も between an adverbial adjective and a negative makes the rejection emphatic. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない both work; 寂しくはない is the more common form. Same trick: 食べたくもない ('I have no wish to eat'), 行きたくもない ('I have zero desire to go').
explanation.es: Insertar も entre adjetivo adverbial y negativo hace el rechazo enfático. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない. Mismo truco: 食べたくもない, 行きたくもない.
explanation.pt-BR: Inserir も entre adjetivo adverbial e negativo torna a rejeição enfática. 寂しくはない → 寂しくもない. Mesmo truque: 食べたくもない, 行きたくもない.

name: Alternation 〜ては〜返す (cyclic action)

explanation.en: Pattern that pairs a verb with another to describe a cyclical alternation. 満ちては返す ('fills-and-returns') — for tides; 行っては来る ('go-and-come') — for travels; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('sink-and-float') — for bobbing. The 〜ては (covered in Redo) marks the recurring 'each time' aspect. Kioku no Umi's 満ちては返す波 ('the wave that fills and returns') is the song's tidal metaphor: memory rises and recedes endlessly.
explanation.es: Patrón que empareja un verbo con otro para describir alternancia cíclica. 満ちては返す ('llenar-y-volver') — para mareas; 行っては来る ('ir-y-venir') — para viajes; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('hundir-y-flotar'). El 〜ては (visto en Redo) marca el aspecto recurrente 'cada vez'. El 満ちては返す波 ('la ola que llena y vuelve') de Kioku no Umi es la metáfora marea-de-memoria: la memoria sube y retrocede sin fin.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão que pareia um verbo com outro pra descrever alternância cíclica. 満ちては返す ('encher-e-voltar') — pra marés; 行っては来る ('ir-e-vir') — viagens; 沈んでは浮かぶ ('afundar-e-flutuar'). O 〜ては (visto em Redo) marca o aspecto recorrente 'cada vez'. O 満ちては返す波 ('a onda que enche e volta') do Kioku no Umi é a metáfora maré-de-memória: a memória sobe e recua sem fim.

name: Backhanded compliment 〜にしては (for / considering it's a)

explanation.en: Pattern: noun + にしては = 'considering it's a [noun] / for a [noun].' Sets up an expectation based on the noun, then lets the predicate exceed (or underperform) it. 子供にしては大人っぽい ('mature for a child / considering she's a child, mature'); 初心者にしては上手 ('skilled for a beginner'). Hizamazuke's 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか = 'for a pig bastard — not bad,' the textbook backhanded compliment.
explanation.es: Patrón: sustantivo + にしては = 'considerando que es un/a [sustantivo] / para un/a [sustantivo]'. Establece expectativa basada en el sustantivo, luego deja al predicado superarla (o no llegar). 子供にしては大人っぽい ('madura para ser una niña'); 初心者にしては上手 ('hábil para ser principiante'). El 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか de Hizamazuke = 'para un cerdo desgraciado — no está mal', cumplido velado de manual.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão: substantivo + にしては = 'considerando que é um/a [substantivo] / pra um/a [substantivo]'. Estabelece expectativa baseada no substantivo, depois deixa o predicado superar (ou ficar abaixo). 子供にしては大人っぽい ('madura pra uma criança'); 初心者にしては上手 ('habilidoso pra um iniciante'). O 豚野郎にしては やるじゃねぇか do Hizamazuke = 'pra um porco desgraçado — nada mal', elogio enviesado de manual.

name: Casual contraction 〜え / 〜ねぇ (rough masculine)

explanation.en: Vowel collapse in casual / rough masculine speech: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi 'amazing') → 凄え (sugee). 知らない (shiranai) → 知らねぇ (shiranee). 危ない (abunai) → 危ねぇ (abunee). The -ee forms signal: blue-collar / shounen anime / tough-guy register. Heard in delinquent characters, sports anime, working-class dialogue. Don't use in polite or even neutral speech — but absolutely standard in shounen battle songs.
explanation.es: Colapso vocálico en habla casual / masculina áspera: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi) → 凄え (sugee). 知らない → 知らねぇ. 危ない → 危ねぇ. Las formas -ee señalan: registro obrero / shounen / tipo duro. Se oyen en personajes delincuentes, animes deportivos, habla obrera. No uses en habla cortés ni neutra — pero estándar absoluto en canciones de batalla shounen.
explanation.pt-BR: Colapso vocálico na fala casual / masculina bruta: -ai → -ee. 凄い (sugoi) → 凄え (sugee). 知らない → 知らねぇ. 危ない → 危ねぇ. As formas -ee sinalizam: registro de operário / shounen / cara durão. Ouvido em personagens delinquentes, animes esportivos, fala de trabalhador. Não use em fala educada nem neutra — mas absolutamente padrão em músicas de batalha shounen.

name: Casual contraction 〜ちゃ / 〜じゃ (= 〜ては / 〜では)

explanation.en: In casual speech, 〜ては contracts to 〜ちゃ and 〜では contracts to 〜じゃ. Common pattern: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('end up doing'). Rarer pattern: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('haven't done / am not doing'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('I haven't given up') — the は inside collapses into ちゃ. Marker of confident, blue-collar masculine register.
explanation.es: En habla casual, 〜ては se contrae a 〜ちゃ y 〜では se contrae a 〜じゃ. Patrón común: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('terminar haciendo'). Más raro: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('no he hecho / no estoy haciendo'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('no me he rendido') — el は del medio colapsa en ちゃ. Marca de registro masculino casual, confiado.
explanation.pt-BR: Na fala casual, 〜ては contrai pra 〜ちゃ e 〜では contrai pra 〜じゃ. Padrão comum: 〜ちゃう = 〜てしまう ('acabar fazendo'). Mais raro: 〜ちゃいない = 〜てはいない ('não tenho/estou fazendo'). 諦めちゃいない = 諦めてはいない ('não desisti') — o は do meio colapsa em ちゃ. Marca de registro masculino casual, confiante.

name: Casual contraction 〜ちゃえば (= 〜てしまえば)

explanation.en: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう ('end up doing'); conditional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('if you just go ahead and do X'). 目をつぶっちゃえば ('if you just close your eyes'). The contraction adds a 'just go for it' feeling.
explanation.es: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう; condicional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('si vas y haces X de una'). 目をつぶっちゃえば. La contracción añade tono de 'hazlo y ya'.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう; condicional 〜てしまえば → 〜ちゃえば ('se você simplesmente fizer X'). 目をつぶっちゃえば. A contração dá tom de 'vai logo fazer'.

name: Casual contractions (わかんない, やっぱ, どっか, ポッケ)

explanation.en: The song is saturated with casual spoken contractions: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット), メトル (= メートル). These give the speaker a young, conversational voice. Learners should recognize them in speech and anime but avoid them in formal writing.
explanation.es: La canción está llena de contracciones habladas: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dan un tono joven y coloquial. Reconocerlas en habla/anime, pero evitarlas en escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: A música é cheia de contrações da fala cotidiana: わかんない (= わからない), やっぱ (= やっぱり), どっか (= どこか), ポッケ (= ポケット). Dão voz jovem e coloquial. Reconhecer em fala/anime, mas evitar em escrita formal.

name: Casual contractions in spoken Japanese

explanation.en: Spoken Japanese drops syllables: している → してる ('doing'), していられない → してらんない ('can't keep doing'), でしょう → でしょ ('right?'), そのとき → そんとき ('at that time'). YUI's lyrics here use these heavily — read them as the longer formal versions.
explanation.es: El japonés hablado omite sílabas: している → してる, していられない → してらんない ('no puedo seguir'), でしょう → でしょ ('¿no?'), そのとき → そんとき ('en ese momento'). YUI usa mucho esto — léelas como la forma larga.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês falado omite sílabas: している → してる, していられない → してらんない ('não dá pra continuar'), でしょう → でしょ ('né?'), そのとき → そんとき ('nessa hora'). As letras de YUI usam muito isso — leia como a forma longa.

name: Casual reasoning 〜もん (because — colloquial)

explanation.en: Sentence-final particle from もの ('thing'). Used in casual speech to give an emotional reason / excuse: 'because (it is the way it is).' Slightly childish or feminine register, but heard widely in shounen and pop. Chozetsu Dynamic's 'ないもん' = 'because there isn't.' Compare 〜から (more neutral 'because') and 〜ので (more formal). The 〜もん softens declarations into 'this is just how it is, you see.'
explanation.es: Partícula final que viene de もの ('cosa'). En habla casual da razón / excusa emocional: 'porque (así son las cosas)'. Registro un poco infantil o femenino, pero se oye en shounen y pop. El 'ないもん' de Chozetsu Dynamic = 'porque no hay'. Compara con 〜から (más neutro 'porque') y 〜ので (más formal). El 〜もん suaviza declaraciones a 'así son las cosas, ¿sabes?'.
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula final vinda de もの ('coisa'). Na fala casual dá razão / desculpa emocional: 'porque (é assim mesmo)'. Registro um pouco infantil ou feminino, mas ouvido em shounen e pop. O 'ないもん' do Chozetsu Dynamic = 'porque não tem'. Compare com 〜から (mais neutro 'porque') e 〜ので (mais formal). O 〜もん abranda declarações em 'é só assim, sabe'.

name: Casual ら抜き / 〜らんない (rough male contraction)

explanation.en: Two contractions of the negative potential 〜られない: 信じれる ('can believe') drops the ら (the 'standard ら抜き form'); 生きらんない ('can't live') compresses 生きられない further into 〜らんない. やってらんない ('can't keep doing this') is the most famous example. All very casual, very masculine.
explanation.es: Dos contracciones del potencial negativo 〜られない: 信じれる ('poder creer') elimina la ら ('forma ら抜き'); 生きらんない ('no poder vivir') comprime aún más 生きられない en 〜らんない. やってらんない es el caso más conocido.
explanation.pt-BR: Duas contrações do potencial negativo 〜られない: 信じれる ('conseguir acreditar') corta o ら ('forma ら抜き'); 生きらんない ('não conseguir viver') comprime ainda mais 生きられない em 〜らんない. やってらんない é o caso mais famoso.

name: Cinematic stacking of te-forms

explanation.en: Stacking te-forms with no other connector creates a sequence of states or actions: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて ('losing, noticing, screaming, struggling'). Each te-form leads to the next without explicit 'then'. Common in lyrics for cinematic, beat-by-beat scenes.
explanation.es: Apilar formas -te sin otro conector crea una secuencia: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて. Cada -te lleva a la siguiente sin un 'luego' explícito. En letras, da un efecto cinematográfico.
explanation.pt-BR: Empilhar formas -te sem outro conector cria sequência: 無くして 気づいて 叫んで もがいて. Cada -te leva à próxima sem 'então' explícito. Em letras, dá efeito cinematográfico.

name: Classical 〜し (literary past)

explanation.en: Bungo (classical Japanese) past attributive ending — modern equivalent is 〜た. Used to give a verse the gravity of an old chronicle. 討ち取りし勇者 (literally 'the hero who slew') would be 討ち取った勇者 in modern Japanese. Modern songs sprinkle it for archaic flavor; using it everywhere would sound stilted, but a single 〜し in an opening verse signals 'this is myth-time.'
explanation.es: Final atributivo de pasado del japonés clásico (bungo) — equivalente moderno es 〜た. Se usa para dar peso de crónica antigua. 討ち取りし勇者 ('el héroe que abatió') sería 討ち取った勇者 hoy. Las canciones modernas lo usan en pequeñas dosis para sabor arcaico; usarlo todo el tiempo sonaría forzado, pero un solo 〜し en el verso inicial señala 'esto es tiempo mítico'.
explanation.pt-BR: Final atributivo de passado do japonês clássico (bungo) — equivalente moderno é 〜た. Usado para dar peso de crônica antiga. 討ち取りし勇者 ('o herói que abateu') seria 討ち取った勇者 hoje. Músicas modernas usam um pouquinho para sabor arcaico; usar sempre soaria forçado, mas um único 〜し no verso inicial sinaliza 'isto é tempo de mito'.

name: Classical/literary endings: 〜き〜かな

explanation.en: い-adjective + き (instead of い) is the classical attributive form, and かな is a literary exclamation (≈ '...alas!' / 'how X!'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ 'how disconsolate it is, alas'. Reserved for poetry, song lyrics, and formal writing for emotional weight.
explanation.es: Adjetivo い + き (en lugar de い) es la forma atributiva clásica, y かな es exclamación literaria (≈ '¡ay, qué...!'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ '¡qué melancolía tan inconsolable!'. Reservado a poesía, letras y escritura formal.
explanation.pt-BR: Adjetivo い + き (em vez de い) é a forma atributiva clássica, e かな é exclamação literária (≈ 'ai... que'). 遣る瀬無きかな ≈ 'que melancolia inconsolável!'. Reservado para poesia, letras e escrita formal.

name: Comparative 〜より + adverb (X-er than)

explanation.en: Pattern: noun + より + adverb + verb = 'V more [adverb] than [noun].' 誰より早く ('faster than anyone'), 何より大切 ('more important than anything'). Adding も to より emphasizes: 誰よりも早く ('faster than even anyone'). longing's 誰よりも早く辿り着く ('arrive faster than anyone') competes with the universal class — the strongest claim available.
explanation.es: Patrón: sustantivo + より + adverbio + verbo = 'V más [adverbio] que [sustantivo]'. 誰より早く ('más rápido que nadie'), 何より大切 ('más importante que nada'). Añadir も a より enfatiza: 誰よりも早く ('más rápido aun que nadie'). El 誰よりも早く辿り着く ('llegar más rápido que nadie') de longing compite con la clase universal — la afirmación más fuerte disponible.
explanation.pt-BR: Padrão: substantivo + より + advérbio + verbo = 'V mais [advérbio] que [substantivo]'. 誰より早く ('mais rápido que qualquer um'), 何より大切 ('mais importante que tudo'). Adicionar も a より enfatiza: 誰よりも早く ('mais rápido até que qualquer um'). O 誰よりも早く辿り着く ('chegar mais rápido que qualquer um') do longing compete com a classe universal — a afirmação mais forte disponível.

name: Comparative 〜より + 〜が + adjective

explanation.en: Standard comparison structure. 'A は B より [adj]' = 'A is [adj]-er than B.' Phoenix uses an inverted version: '勝利の味は 楽勝より 悪戦苦闘の末が美味' = literally 'victory's taste, easy-win-than fierce-struggle's-end (subj) delicious' = 'victory tastes more delicious at the end of a fierce struggle than from an easy win.' The 〜より marks the standard being beaten; the 〜が marks the new winner; the adjective gives the criterion.
explanation.es: Estructura de comparación estándar. 'A は B より [adj]' = 'A es más [adj] que B'. Phoenix usa una versión invertida: '勝利の味は 楽勝より 悪戦苦闘の末が美味' = 'el sabor de la victoria, más que la victoria fácil, el fin del combate duro es delicioso'. 〜より marca el estándar superado; 〜が marca al nuevo ganador; el adjetivo da el criterio.
explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura de comparação padrão. 'A は B より [adj]' = 'A é mais [adj] que B'. Phoenix usa versão invertida: '勝利の味は 楽勝より 悪戦苦闘の末が美味' = 'sabor da vitória, mais que a vitória fácil, o fim da luta árdua é delicioso'. 〜より marca o padrão derrotado; 〜が marca o novo vencedor; o adjetivo dá o critério.

name: Compound imperative 〜してゆけ / 〜していけ

explanation.en: Imperative form of compound 〜てゆく / 〜ていく ('go on V-ing'). Combine te-form + ゆく/いく + imperative ending: 残してゆけ ('go on leaving / leave behind as you go'). The 〜ゆく vs 〜いく choice is register: ゆく is literary, いく is everyday. The compound captures both the action (leaving) and the trajectory (departing). Smile for you uses そっと残してゆけ ('gently leave it behind, going') as the song's farewell instruction.
explanation.es: Forma imperativa del compuesto 〜てゆく / 〜ていく ('seguir V-ando'). Combina te-forma + ゆく/いく + final imperativo: 残してゆけ ('ve dejando / déjalo al partir'). La elección 〜ゆく vs 〜いく es registro: ゆく es literario, いく es cotidiano. El compuesto captura tanto la acción como la trayectoria. Smile for you usa そっと残してゆけ como instrucción de despedida.
explanation.pt-BR: Forma imperativa do composto 〜てゆく / 〜ていく ('continuar V-ando'). Combina forma-te + ゆく/いく + final imperativo: 残してゆけ ('vá deixando / deixe ao partir'). A escolha 〜ゆく vs 〜いく é registro: ゆく é literário, いく é cotidiano. O composto captura tanto a ação quanto a trajetória. Smile for you usa そっと残してゆけ como instrução de despedida.

name: Compound stem chaining 〜続け (keep V-ing — stem form)

explanation.en: Verb stem + 続ける = 'keep V-ing' (covered in Styx Helix). Hands Up! uses the stem-form 〜続け to chain to the next clause: 信じ続け 突き進んできた ('kept believing, came charging forward'). This is the 連用形 'and' form — the 続け acts as the conjunction between two verbs without needing 〜て or another connector. Allows densely stacked verbs in a single line.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 続ける = 'seguir V' (visto en Styx Helix). Hands Up! usa la raíz 〜続け para encadenar al verso siguiente: 信じ続け 突き進んできた ('seguimos creyendo, vinimos avanzando'). Es la forma-conjunción 連用形 — el 続け sirve de unión entre verbos sin necesitar 〜て. Permite verbos densamente apilados en una línea.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz do verbo + 続ける = 'continuar V' (visto em Styx Helix). Hands Up! usa a raiz 〜続け pra encadear pro próximo verso: 信じ続け 突き進んできた ('continuamos acreditando, fomos avançando com força'). Esta é a forma-conjunção 連用形 — o 続け serve como ligação entre verbos sem precisar de 〜て. Permite verbos densamente empilhados numa linha.

name: Compound stem-form chains (V-stem + V-stem)

explanation.en: Japanese stacks verbs by attaching one verb's stem (連用形) to another. Linked Horizon uses several: 包み込む (包む 'wrap' + 込む 'into'), 立ち向かう (立つ 'stand' + 向かう 'face'), 染める (already a base verb, but combines with 赤く). Each compound carries a distinct meaning the simple verb doesn't: 包む ('wrap') vs 包み込む ('completely envelop'); 向かう ('face') vs 立ち向かう ('stand against'). Learn compound verbs as units, not as the sum of their parts.
explanation.es: El japonés apila verbos uniendo la raíz (連用形) de un verbo a otro. Linked Horizon usa varios: 包み込む (包む 'envolver' + 込む 'hacia dentro'), 立ち向かう (立つ 'estar de pie' + 向かう 'enfrentar'). Cada compuesto trae un sentido distinto que el verbo simple no tiene: 包む ('envolver') vs 包み込む ('envolver del todo'); 向かう ('enfrentar') vs 立ち向かう ('plantarse ante'). Aprende los verbos compuestos como unidades, no como suma de partes.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês empilha verbos ligando a raiz (連用形) de um verbo a outro. Linked Horizon usa vários: 包み込む (包む 'envolver' + 込む 'pra dentro'), 立ち向かう (立つ 'ficar de pé' + 向かう 'enfrentar'). Cada composto traz um sentido distinto que o verbo simples não tem: 包む ('envolver') vs 包み込む ('envolver completamente'); 向かう ('enfrentar') vs 立ち向かう ('ficar de pé contra'). Aprenda verbos compostos como unidades, não soma das partes.

name: Compound suffix 〜出す (begin / set out)

explanation.en: Verb stem + 出す = 'begin V-ing / set out doing.' Two flavors: (1) 'begin suddenly / break into' (走り出す 'break into a run,' 笑い出す 'burst out laughing,' 泣き出す 'start crying'); (2) 'come out / produce' (作り出す 'create-out,' 思い出す 'recall'). Glory Days's 歩き出そう ('let's set out walking') is sense (1) — beginning the walk that ends the song. Pairs naturally with 〜よう volitional.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 出す = 'empezar a V / echarse a hacer'. Dos matices: (1) 'empezar súbitamente / echarse a' (走り出す 'echarse a correr,' 笑い出す 'soltar la risa,' 泣き出す 'romper a llorar'); (2) 'sacar / producir' (作り出す 'crear-sacar,' 思い出す 'recordar'). El 歩き出そう ('echémonos a andar') de Glory Days es (1) — empezar la caminata que cierra la canción. Combina natural con volitivo 〜よう.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz do verbo + 出す = 'começar a V / partir fazendo'. Dois sentidos: (1) 'começar de repente / irromper' (走り出す 'sair correndo,' 笑い出す 'começar a rir,' 泣き出す 'cair no choro'); (2) 'sair / produzir' (作り出す 'criar,' 思い出す 'lembrar de'). O 歩き出そう ('vamos começar a caminhar') do Glory Days é (1) — começar a caminhada que encerra a música. Combina natural com volitivo 〜よう.

name: Compound suffix 〜抜ける (race / pass through)

explanation.en: Verb stem + 抜ける = 'V through (and out the other side).' The 〜抜ける suffix adds 'completely traverse / pass through.' 駆ける ('gallop / race') + 抜ける = 駆け抜ける ('race through'); 通る ('pass') + 抜ける = 通り抜ける ('pass through'); 突き抜ける ('break through'); 走り抜ける ('run through'). Ryuusei's 駆け抜ける describes a meteor crossing the night sky end-to-end — the most cinematic verb available.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 抜ける = 'V atravesando (y saliendo del otro lado)'. El sufijo 〜抜ける añade 'atravesar por completo / pasar a través'. 駆ける ('galopar / correr') + 抜ける = 駆け抜ける ('atravesar corriendo'); 通る + 抜ける = 通り抜ける ('pasar a través'); 突き抜ける ('romper'); 走り抜ける ('correr a través'). El 駆け抜ける de Ryuusei describe un meteoro cruzando el cielo de extremo a extremo — el verbo más cinematográfico disponible.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz do verbo + 抜ける = 'V atravessando (e saindo do outro lado)'. O sufixo 〜抜ける adiciona 'atravessar por completo / passar através'. 駆ける ('galopar / correr') + 抜ける = 駆け抜ける ('atravessar correndo'); 通る + 抜ける = 通り抜ける ('passar através'); 突き抜ける ('romper'); 走り抜ける ('correr através'). O 駆け抜ける do Ryuusei descreve meteoro cortando o céu de ponta a ponta — verbo mais cinematográfico possível.

name: Compound suffix 〜込む (deeply / into)

explanation.en: Verb stem + 込む adds the sense of 'V into / V deeply / V completely.' Productive in Japanese: 飲み込む ('swallow down,' 飲む + 込む), 思い込む ('be convinced,' 思う + 込む), 信じ込む ('believe deeply'), 刻み込む ('engrave deeply,' 刻む + 込む). The 込む adds intensification or directionality (into a container, into the body, into memory). Hands Up!'s 刻み込んだ uses it for 'carved DEEP into' the chest.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 込む añade el sentido 'V hacia dentro / V profundamente / V por completo'. Productivo: 飲み込む ('tragar,' 飲む + 込む), 思い込む ('quedarse convencido'), 信じ込む ('creer profundamente'), 刻み込む ('grabar profundamente'). El 込む añade intensificación o dirección (hacia dentro de un recipiente, del cuerpo, de la memoria). El 刻み込んだ de Hands Up! lo usa para 'grabar HONDO' en el pecho.
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz do verbo + 込む adiciona o sentido 'V para dentro / V profundamente / V por completo'. Produtivo: 飲み込む ('engolir,' 飲む + 込む), 思い込む ('ficar convencido'), 信じ込む ('acreditar profundamente'), 刻み込む ('gravar profundamente'). O 込む adiciona intensificação ou direção (para dentro de container, corpo, memória). O 刻み込んだ do Hands Up! usa pra 'gravar FUNDO' no peito.

name: Compound verb suffix 〜抜く / 〜出す

explanation.en: Japanese stacks verbs by attaching one verb's stem (連用形) to another. 〜抜く = 'do completely / see through' (守り抜く = 'protect through to the end'). 〜出す = 'bring out / start V-ing suddenly' (作り出す = 'create/produce out'; 切り出す = 'cut out / quarry out'). These suffixes give a single Japanese verb the meaning English would use a phrasal verb for ('protect-through,' 'cut-out').
explanation.es: El japonés apila verbos uniendo la raíz (連用形) de un verbo a otro. 〜抜く = 'hacer hasta el final' (守り抜く = 'proteger hasta el final'). 〜出す = 'sacar / empezar súbitamente' (作り出す = 'crear/producir'; 切り出す = 'recortar'). Estos sufijos dan a un verbo japonés el sentido que en español se expresa con locución.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês empilha verbos ligando a raiz (連用形) de um verbo a outro. 〜抜く = 'fazer até o fim' (守り抜く = 'proteger até o fim'). 〜出す = 'fazer sair / começar de repente' (作り出す = 'criar/produzir'; 切り出す = 'recortar'). Esses sufixos dão a um verbo japonês o sentido que o português normalmente expressa com locução.

name: Compound verb suffix 〜抜く / 〜出す / 〜寄せる

explanation.en: Japanese stacks verbs by attaching one verb's stem (連用形) to another. 〜抜く = 'do completely / see through to the end' (守り抜く 'protect to the end'). 〜出す = 'bring out / start V-ing' (救い出す 'rescue out,' 走り出す 'break into a run'). 〜寄せる = 'draw toward' (手繰り寄せる 'draw in by hand'). These suffixes give a single Japanese verb the meaning English would express with phrasal verbs ('protect-through,' 'rescue-out,' 'pull-toward').
explanation.es: El japonés apila verbos uniendo la raíz (連用形) de un verbo a otro. 〜抜く = 'hacer hasta el final' (守り抜く 'proteger hasta el final'). 〜出す = 'sacar / empezar' (救い出す 'rescatar sacando', 走り出す 'echar a correr'). 〜寄せる = 'tirar hacia' (手繰り寄せる 'tirar mano sobre mano'). Estos sufijos dan a un verbo japonés el sentido que el español expresa con locución.
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês empilha verbos ligando a raiz (連用形) de um verbo a outro. 〜抜く = 'fazer até o fim' (守り抜く 'proteger até o fim'). 〜出す = 'fazer sair / começar' (救い出す 'resgatar tirando', 走り出す 'sair correndo'). 〜寄せる = 'puxar em direção a' (手繰り寄せる 'puxar mão por mão'). Esses sufixos dão a um verbo japonês o sentido que o português normalmente expressa com locução.

name: Compound verbs (literary completion / direction)

explanation.en:
Japanese stitches verbs together by attaching one verb's i-stem (連用形) to another verb. The second verb adds nuance — direction, completeness, intensity. This creates dense, literary expressions.

This song packs compound verbs into nearly every line: 踏み出す (step + out), 吸い込む (suck + deeply-in), 追い越す (chase + go-beyond), 過ぎ去る (pass + go-away), 振り上げる (swing + up), 掴み取る (grab + take), 解き放つ (untie + release), 飛び越える (fly + cross), 見つけ出す (find + bring-out), 曝け出す (expose + bring-out).

Other typical compound suffixes:
 - 〜出す (start; bring out): 走り出す ('break into a run')
 - 〜込む (deeply / inward): 飲み込む ('swallow whole')
 - 〜越す / 〜越える (go past): 乗り越える ('overcome')
 - 〜抜く (do thoroughly): やり抜く ('see through to the end')
 - 〜放つ (release): 解き放つ ('set free')
 - 〜上げる (raise up): 振り上げる ('swing aloft')

name: Compound verbs of penetration (超える / 貫く / 届く)

explanation.en: Three verbs that map a feeling's trajectory: 超える ('surpass / cross over' — used for limits, time, oneself), 貫く ('pierce / penetrate / shoot through'), 届く ('reach / arrive at'). Ubiquitous dB chains all three in its closing verse — 時間を超え 胸を貫き 心に届く ('surpassing time, piercing the chest, reaching the heart'). The progression is locational: time → chest → heart, each verb getting more intimate.
explanation.es: Tres verbos que trazan la trayectoria de un sentimiento: 超える ('sobrepasar / cruzar' — usado para límites, tiempo, uno mismo), 貫く ('atravesar / penetrar de lado a lado'), 届く ('llegar / arribar'). El Ubiquitous dB encadena los tres en el verso final — 時間を超え 胸を貫き 心に届く ('cruzando el tiempo, atravesando el pecho, llegando al corazón'). La progresión es locacional: tiempo → pecho → corazón, cada verbo más íntimo.
explanation.pt-BR: Três verbos que mapeiam a trajetória de um sentimento: 超える ('superar / atravessar' — usado pra limites, tempo, si mesmo), 貫く ('perfurar / atravessar de lado a lado'), 届く ('alcançar / chegar'). O Ubiquitous dB encadeia os três no verso final — 時間を超え 胸を貫き 心に届く ('atravessando o tempo, perfurando o peito, chegando ao coração'). A progressão é locacional: tempo → peito → coração, cada verbo mais íntimo.

name: Compound verbs with 〜落ちる / 〜潰す / 〜絞る (verb + verb)

explanation.en:
Japanese freely joins verbs by attaching the second verb to the stem form of the first. The second verb modifies how the first happens.

Examples from this song:
• 剥がれ落ちる (hagareochiru) = 剥がれる (peel) + 落ちる (fall) = 'peel off and fall'
• 塗り潰す (nuritsubusu) = 塗る (paint) + 潰す (crush/flatten) = 'paint out completely'
• 振り絞る (furishiboru) = 振る (shake) + 絞る (wring) = 'wring out with effort'
• 忍び寄る (shinobiyoru) = 忍ぶ (sneak) + 寄る (approach) = 'creep up'

The second verb often answers 'how / how thoroughly' — crushed, wrung, sneakily, etc.

name: Compound verbs with 〜込む (do thoroughly / deeply)

explanation.en:
Attaching 込む to a verb's i-stem creates a compound that adds a sense of 'doing the action thoroughly, deeply, or inward'. The closing verb 込む originally means 'to crowd into' or 'to pack in', and that physical/emotional 'in-ness' colours every compound.

This song uses 包みこんで in 悲しみも痛みも包みこんで ('wrap up the sadness and the pain too' — completely, deeply). Plain 包む is 'to wrap'; 包み込む intensifies it: not a paper wrapper, but a full embrace of pain.

Other typical examples with 〜込む: 飲み込む ('to swallow / take in completely'), 落ち込む ('to fall into / become depressed'), 思い込む ('to convince oneself firmly'), 信じ込む ('to believe deeply').

name: Compound verbs 〜落ちる / 〜去る / 〜乗せる (verb + verb compounds)

explanation.en:
Japanese freely combines two verbs by attaching the second to the stem form of the first. The combined verb carries nuances from both parts.

Examples from this song:
• 剥がれ落ちた (hagareochita) = 剥がれる (peel off) + 落ちる (fall) = 'peeled off and fell'
• 生まれ落ちた (umareochita) = 生まれる (be born) + 落ちる (fall) = 'came into being' (literary)
• 奪い去る (ubaisaru) = 奪う (snatch) + 去る (leave) = 'snatch away and vanish'

More examples:
• 書き込む (write into — write + enter)
• 歩き回る (walk around — walk + go around)
• 食べ過ぎる (overeat — eat + exceed)

The second verb often tells you how or how thoroughly the action happens.

name: Compound 〜打ち明ける (open up about / reveal)

explanation.en: Compound verb: 打つ ('strike / pound') + 明ける ('open / reveal'). Means 'open up about a hidden feeling / confess.' The 打ち prefix in compound verbs adds force or completeness — 打ち明ける = 'forcibly open up,' more emphatic than just 言う ('say'). Other 打ち〜 compounds: 打ち消す ('disprove / negate'), 打ち破る ('shatter / break through'), 打ち込む ('drive into / be absorbed in'). Niji no Sora's 痛み打ち明けてくれた人 ('the person who confided pain to me') uses it for the courageous act of revealing.
explanation.es: Verbo compuesto: 打つ ('golpear') + 明ける ('abrir / revelar'). Significa 'abrirse sobre un sentimiento oculto / confesar'. El prefijo 打ち en verbos compuestos añade fuerza o completitud — 打ち明ける = 'abrir con fuerza', más enfático que solo 言う ('decir'). Otros compuestos 打ち〜: 打ち消す ('desmentir'), 打ち破る ('romper'), 打ち込む ('clavar / dedicarse'). El 痛み打ち明けてくれた人 de Niji no Sora lo usa para el acto valiente de revelar.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo composto: 打つ ('bater / golpear') + 明ける ('abrir / revelar'). Significa 'abrir-se sobre sentimento escondido / confessar'. O prefixo 打ち em verbos compostos adiciona força ou completude — 打ち明ける = 'abrir com força', mais enfático que só 言う ('dizer'). Outros compostos 打ち〜: 打ち消す ('desmentir'), 打ち破る ('quebrar'), 打ち込む ('cravar / dedicar-se'). O 痛み打ち明けてくれた人 do Niji no Sora usa pra o ato corajoso de revelar.

name: Compound 〜抜く (V through to the end)

explanation.en: Verb stem + 抜く = 'V through to absolute completion / V no matter what.' The 〜抜く suffix conveys 'see it through despite obstacles.' Common compounds: 守り抜く ('protect to the end' — Yuusha), 戦い抜く ('fight through' — Phoenix), 信じ抜く ('believe through' — Niji no Sora). The imperative 〜抜け ('see V through!') is what the song uses: 信じ抜け ('keep believing through'). Different from 〜抜ける (intransitive 'pass through'), which describes the passing without the resolve.
explanation.es: Raíz del verbo + 抜く = 'V hasta el final absoluto / V pase lo que pase'. El sufijo 〜抜く transmite 'llevar hasta el final pese a obstáculos'. Compuestos comunes: 守り抜く ('proteger hasta el final' — Yuusha), 戦い抜く ('luchar hasta el final' — Phoenix), 信じ抜く ('creer hasta el final' — Niji no Sora). El imperativo 〜抜け ('¡lleva V hasta el final!') es el que usa la canción: 信じ抜け. Distinto de 〜抜ける (intransitivo 'atravesar pasando').
explanation.pt-BR: Raiz do verbo + 抜く = 'V até o fim absoluto / V não importa o que'. O sufixo 〜抜く transmite 'levar até o fim apesar dos obstáculos'. Compostos comuns: 守り抜く ('proteger até o fim' — Yuusha), 戦い抜く ('lutar até o fim' — Phoenix), 信じ抜く ('acreditar até o fim' — Niji no Sora). O imperativo 〜抜け ('leve V até o fim!') é o que a música usa: 信じ抜け. Diferente de 〜抜ける (intransitivo 'atravessar passando').

name: Compound 〜暴く (literary 'expose')

explanation.en: Verb 暴く ('expose / uncover what's hidden'). Literary register — used for digging up scandals, revealing secrets, breaking seals on truth. Common compounds: 暴き出す ('drag out into the open'), 暴き立てる ('expose dramatically / publicly'). Pairs with 〜てみせる for the determined 'expose, you'll see' construction. Distinct from 明かす ('reveal / declare' — covered in Scar): 明かす is voluntary disclosure; 暴く is forceful exposure of what was being hidden.
explanation.es: Verbo 暴く ('exponer / desvelar lo oculto'). Registro literario — para destapar escándalos, revelar secretos, romper sellos sobre la verdad. Compuestos comunes: 暴き出す ('sacar a la luz'), 暴き立てる ('exponer dramáticamente'). Empareja con 〜てみせる para la construcción decidida 'exponer, ya verás'. Distinto de 明かす ('revelar / declarar' — visto en Scar): 明かす es divulgación voluntaria; 暴く es exposición forzada de lo que se ocultaba.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo 暴く ('expor / desvelar o que está escondido'). Registro literário — usado pra desencavar escândalos, revelar segredos, quebrar selos da verdade. Compostos comuns: 暴き出す ('arrastar pra fora'), 暴き立てる ('expor dramaticamente'). Combina com 〜てみせる pra construção determinada 'expor, vai ver'. Distinto de 明かす ('revelar / declarar' — visto em Scar): 明かす é divulgação voluntária; 暴く é exposição forçada do que estava sendo escondido.

name: Compound 見透かす (see through)

explanation.en: Compound verb: 見る ('see') + 透かす ('make transparent / hold up to the light'). Means 'see through (someone's intentions, lies, weaknesses).' The 透 ('transparent') is the same kanji in 透ける ('be transparent'). Common pattern V1 + V2 where V1 is the action and V2 modifies how: 見透かす, 見破る ('see-tear' = see through a deception), 見抜く ('see-pull-out' = perceive deeply). Rapport: '僕の弱さを見透かしていた' = 'you had seen through my weakness.'
explanation.es: Verbo compuesto: 見る ('ver') + 透かす ('hacer transparente'). Significa 'ver a través (de las intenciones, mentiras, debilidades)'. El 透 es el mismo kanji de 透ける ('ser transparente'). Patrón común V1 + V2 donde V1 es la acción y V2 modifica el cómo: 見透かす, 見破る ('ver-romper' = ver a través de un engaño), 見抜く ('ver-extraer' = percibir hondo). Rapport: '僕の弱さを見透かしていた' = 'habías visto a través de mi debilidad'.
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo composto: 見る ('ver') + 透かす ('tornar transparente'). Significa 'ver através (das intenções, mentiras, fraquezas)'. O 透 é o mesmo kanji de 透ける ('ser transparente'). Padrão comum V1 + V2 onde V1 é a ação e V2 modifica o como: 見透かす, 見破る ('ver-rasgar' = ver através de um engano), 見抜く ('ver-puxar-fora' = perceber fundo). Rapport: '僕の弱さを見透かしていた' = 'você tinha visto através da minha fraqueza'.

name: Concession 〜たって / どんなに〜たって

explanation.en: 〜たって is the casual contraction of 〜ても ('even if'). Often paired with どんなに ('however much') for absolute concession: 'no matter how much I V.' Ryuusei's 'どんなに願ったって' = 'no matter how much I wish.' The pattern stresses that the wishing-or-not has no bearing on what comes next. Compare with もっと願っても ('even if I wish more') — どんなに intensifies the quantifier.
explanation.es: 〜たって es la contracción casual de 〜ても ('aunque'). Frecuente con どんなに ('por mucho que') para concesión absoluta: 'por mucho que V'. El 'どんなに願ったって' de Ryuusei = 'por mucho que desee'. El patrón enfatiza que el desear-o-no no influye en lo que sigue. Compara con もっと願っても ('aunque desee más') — どんなに intensifica el cuantificador.
explanation.pt-BR: 〜たって é contração casual de 〜ても ('mesmo que'). Frequente com どんなに ('por mais que') pra concessão absoluta: 'por mais que eu V'. O 'どんなに願ったって' do Ryuusei = 'por mais que eu deseje'. O padrão estressa que o desejar-ou-não não influencia no que vem depois. Compare com もっと願っても ('mesmo que eu deseje mais') — どんなに intensifica o quantificador.

name: Conditional stack: 〜てしまえたら ('if I could fully X')

explanation.en: Three layers: 〜てしまう ('do completely / end up doing') + 〜える (potential 'be able to') + 〜たら (conditional). 消してしまえたら = 'if I could erase it once and for all'; 泣いてしまえたら = 'if I could just go ahead and cry'. Common pattern for a wished-for completed action.
explanation.es: Tres capas: 〜てしまう ('hacer del todo') + 〜える (potencial) + 〜たら (condicional). 消してしまえたら = 'si pudiera borrarlo del todo'; 泣いてしまえたら = 'si pudiera echarme a llorar y ya'.
explanation.pt-BR: Três camadas: 〜てしまう ('fazer por completo') + 〜える (potencial) + 〜たら (condicional). 消してしまえたら = 'se eu pudesse apagar de vez'; 泣いてしまえたら = 'se eu conseguisse simplesmente chorar'.

name: Conditional 〜たら / 〜ば (if / when)

explanation.en: Two ways to say 'if': verb-past + ら (巡りあったら 'if/when we meet again') and verb-conditional ば (閉じれば 'if I close', なければ 'if not'). 〜たら is more concrete/event-based; 〜ば is more general/hypothetical. Both are heavily used in lyrics.
explanation.es: Dos formas de decir 'si': verbo-pasado + ら (巡りあったら 'si nos encontramos de nuevo') y verbo-condicional ば (閉じれば 'si cierro', なければ 'si no'). 〜たら es más concreto/basado en un evento; 〜ば es más general/hipotético.
explanation.pt-BR: Duas formas de dizer 'se': verbo-passado + ら (巡りあったら 'se nos encontrarmos de novo') e verbo-condicional ば (閉じれば 'se eu fechar', なければ 'se não'). 〜たら é mais concreto/baseado em evento; 〜ば é mais geral/hipotético.

name: Conditional 〜ば + はずさ ('should be able to')

explanation.en: Verb-conditional 〜ば ('if X') + potential verb + はず ('should/expected') is a standard 'if I do X, I should be able to Y' construction. 手を伸ばせば 輝けるはず = 'if I reach out, I should be able to shine'. The さ at the end is a softly assertive male sentence-final particle.
explanation.es: Verbo-condicional 〜ば ('si X') + verbo en potencial + はず ('debería') forma la construcción 'si hago X, debería poder Y'. 手を伸ばせば 輝けるはず. La さ final es una partícula de afirmación suave (masculina).
explanation.pt-BR: Verbo-condicional 〜ば ('se X') + verbo no potencial + はず ('deveria') é a construção 'se eu fizer X, deveria conseguir Y'. 手を伸ばせば 輝けるはず. O さ no fim é uma partícula de afirmação suave (mais masculina).

name: Conditional 〜ば → 〜りゃ (slang contraction)

explanation.en:
In rough/casual speech, the 〜ば conditional shrinks to 〜りゃ for Group 2 verbs (the れば → りゃ collapse). Found in old Edo speech, song lyrics, and rural-flavoured dialogue.

This song uses 夢見りゃ叶うよ ('if you dream, it'll come true'). Full form: 夢見れば → 夢見りゃ. The collapse adds folksy swagger.

Other typical examples: 行きゃいい (full: 行けばいい — 'just go'), 食えりゃ食う (full: 食えれば食う — 'if I can eat, I will'), 来りゃ来い (full: 来れば来い — 'if you're coming, come').

name: Contemptuous plural 〜ども

explanation.en: Suffix attached to nouns to form a rough/contemptuous plural. Used for animals, enemies, or despised people: 豚ども ('the pigs'), 奴ども ('those bastards'), 子供ども ('the brats'). Distinct from neutral 〜たち (我々, 子供たち) and -ら (僕ら, 奴ら): 〜ども carries explicit disdain. Common in samurai dramas, military shouting, and pirate / bandit dialogue. The さ at the end of 豚どもが uses が as vocative, NOT subject-marker — addressing the pigs directly.
explanation.es: Sufijo unido a sustantivos para formar plural rudo/despectivo. Usado para animales, enemigos, o personas despreciadas: 豚ども ('los cerdos'), 奴ども ('esos desgraciados'), 子供ども ('los mocosos'). Distinto del neutro 〜たち y -ら: 〜ども lleva desdén explícito. Común en dramas samurái, gritos militares y diálogos de piratas / bandidos. El が al final de 豚どもが usa が como vocativo, NO marcador de sujeto.
explanation.pt-BR: Sufixo ligado a substantivos pra formar plural rude/desdenhoso. Usado pra animais, inimigos, ou pessoas desprezadas: 豚ども ('os porcos'), 奴ども ('aqueles desgraçados'), 子供ども ('os fedelhos'). Distinto do neutro 〜たち e -ら: 〜ども carrega desdém explícito. Comum em dramas samurai, gritaria militar e diálogos de piratas / bandidos. O が no final de 豚どもが usa が como vocativo, NÃO marcador de sujeito.

name: Conveyance verbs of declaration: 告げる / 寄せる / かける

explanation.en: Three verbs for kinds of human gesture toward another person/space. 告げる ('announce / declare formally') — for ceremonial proclamations (winning, ending, announcing the season). 寄せる ('draw close to / lean against') — for both physical leaning and emotional approach. 声をかける ('apply voice' = call out / address) — for initiating speech with someone. The Fourth Avenue Cafe uses all three across the song: declaring the end, leaning into memories, calling to the sky. Each one is a particular shape of unfinished communication.
explanation.es: Tres verbos para tipos de gesto humano hacia otra persona/espacio. 告げる ('anunciar / declarar') — para proclamaciones ceremoniales. 寄せる ('arrimar / acercarse') — para arrimo físico y acercamiento emocional. 声をかける ('aplicar voz' = llamar / interpelar) — para iniciar habla con alguien. El Fourth Avenue Cafe usa los tres a lo largo de la canción: declarar el fin, arrimarse a recuerdos, llamar al cielo. Cada uno es una forma particular de comunicación inacabada.
explanation.pt-BR: Três verbos pra tipos de gesto humano em direção a outra pessoa/espaço. 告げる ('anunciar / declarar') — pra proclamações cerimoniais. 寄せる ('aproximar / encostar') — pra encosto físico e aproximação emocional. 声をかける ('aplicar voz' = chamar / interpelar) — pra iniciar fala com alguém. O Fourth Avenue Cafe usa os três ao longo da música: declarar o fim, encostar em memórias, chamar o céu. Cada um é uma forma particular de comunicação inacabada.

name: Conveyance verbs: 伝える / 届ける / 届く

explanation.en: Three related verbs of message/object transmission, distinguished by transitivity and direction. 伝える ('convey / transmit' — transitive: 'A conveys X to B'). 届ける ('deliver' — transitive: 'A delivers X to B'). 届く ('reach / arrive' — INTRANSITIVE: 'X arrives at B'). Smile for you uses 伝える ('convey the smile') and 届く ('reach the chest') in different verses. Choosing 伝える stresses the agency of the conveyor; 届く stresses the journey of the thing itself.
explanation.es: Tres verbos relacionados de transmisión de mensaje/objeto, distinguidos por transitividad y dirección. 伝える ('transmitir' — transitivo: 'A transmite X a B'). 届ける ('entregar' — transitivo). 届く ('llegar / arribar' — INTRANSITIVO: 'X llega a B'). Smile for you usa 伝える ('transmitir la sonrisa') y 届く ('llegar al pecho'). Elegir 伝える enfatiza la agencia del transmisor; 届く enfatiza el viaje del objeto.
explanation.pt-BR: Três verbos relacionados de transmissão de mensagem/objeto, distinguidos por transitividade e direção. 伝える ('transmitir' — transitivo: 'A transmite X a B'). 届ける ('entregar' — transitivo). 届く ('chegar / arribar' — INTRANSITIVO: 'X chega a B'). Smile for you usa 伝える ('transmitir o sorriso') e 届く ('chegar ao peito'). Escolher 伝える enfatiza a agência de quem transmite; 届く enfatiza a jornada do objeto.

name: Counterfactual 〜たなら / 〜られたなら (if I could / if it had been)

explanation.en: Past-tense conditional structure. Plain past + なら sets up a hypothetical: 'if it had been/were the case that ~.' With potential verbs: 〜られたなら / 〜えたなら ('if I were able to ~'). Kioku no Umi's 進めたなら ('if I could advance') asks a counterfactual: imagining the impossible crossing. The structure leaves the consequence open or fragile (often paired with 〜消えるの? in question form): 'if X, would Y vanish?'
explanation.es: Estructura de condicional en pasado. Pasado simple + なら establece una hipótesis: 'si hubiera sido / si fuera el caso de ~'. Con verbos potenciales: 〜られたなら / 〜えたなら ('si pudiera ~'). El 進めたなら ('si pudiera cruzar') de Kioku no Umi pregunta un contrafáctico: imaginar la travesía imposible. La estructura deja la consecuencia abierta o frágil (frecuente con 〜消えるの? en pregunta): 'si X, ¿desaparecería Y?'.
explanation.pt-BR: Estrutura de condicional no passado. Passado simples + なら estabelece uma hipótese: 'se tivesse sido / se fosse o caso de ~'. Com verbos potenciais: 〜られたなら / 〜えたなら ('se eu pudesse ~'). O 進めたなら ('se eu pudesse atravessar') do Kioku no Umi pergunta um contrafactual: imaginar a travessia impossível. A estrutura deixa a consequência aberta ou frágil (frequente combinada com 〜消えるの? em pergunta): 'se X, será que Y sumiria?'.

name: Counting: cardinal numbers 1-99

explanation.en: Japanese counts 1-10 with native + Sino-Japanese forms, then compounds them: 21 = 二十一 (nijuu-ichi), 99 = 九十九 (kyuujuu-kyuu). The pattern is always [tens-digit] 十 [ones-digit]. 4 (yon) and 7 (nana) are preferred over し/しち in counting because the latter sound like 死 (death) and 質 (pawn).
explanation.es: El japonés cuenta 1-10 con dos series y luego compone: 21 = 二十一, 99 = 九十九. Se prefiere 4 (yon) y 7 (nana) por superstición (し = 死 muerte).
explanation.pt-BR: O japonês conta 1-10 com duas séries, depois compõe: 21 = 二十一, 99 = 九十九 (sempre [dezena] 十 [unidade]). 4 (yon) e 7 (nana) são preferidos em contagem por superstição (し = 死 morte).

name: Dismissive 〜など (= 〜なんて, literary)

explanation.en: など inserted into a clause downplays or dismisses what comes before: 悲しくなどない ('it's not the slightest bit sad'); 不安など消してしまえたら ('if I could erase the anxiety and all that'). More literary than the casual 〜なんて with the same meaning.
explanation.es: など inserido minimiza o despacha lo anterior: 悲しくなどない ('no es ni pizca triste'); 不安など消してしまえたら ('si pudiera borrar la ansiedad y todo eso'). Más literario que el casual 〜なんて.
explanation.pt-BR: など inserido numa cláusula minimiza ou afasta o anterior: 悲しくなどない ('não é nem um pouco triste'); 不安など消してしまえたら ('se pudesse apagar essa ansiedade toda'). Mais literário que o casual 〜なんて.

name: Dismissive 〜なんて

explanation.en: Particle attached to nouns or verb-dictionary forms to mean 'something like ~ / ~ and the like.' Distinctive feature: tone of dismissal or surprise. Listing X with なんて downgrades it: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('applause and the like? — don't want it'). Compare neutral 喝采は欲しくない ('I don't want applause') vs scornful 喝采なんて欲しくない. Often pairs with surprised reaction: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('the fact that you can do it is amazing!').
explanation.es: Partícula unida a sustantivos o verbos en forma de diccionario con sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ y demás'. Marca: tono de desprecio o sorpresa. Listar X con なんて lo rebaja: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovación y esas cosas — no la quiero'). Compara neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. despectivo 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frecuente en reacción de sorpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('¡que puedas hacerlo es increíble!').
explanation.pt-BR: Partícula ligada a substantivos ou verbos na forma de dicionário com sentido 'algo como ~ / ~ e tal'. Marca: tom de desdém ou surpresa. Listar X com なんて desvaloriza: 喝采なんて欲しくはない ('ovação e essas coisas? — não quero'). Compare neutro 喝采は欲しくない vs. desdenhoso 喝采なんて欲しくない. Frequente em reação surpresa: 'できるなんてすごい!' ('o fato de você conseguir é incrível!').

name: Dismissive 〜なんて (things like / something as trivial as)

explanation.en: なんて downplays or distances what comes before: 妬み嫉妬なんてない ('we don't have envy or jealousy or anything like that'); 好きになることなんて分からない ('I don't get this whole falling-in-love thing'). Always carries a slightly dismissive, distancing tone.
explanation.es: なんて resta importancia a lo anterior: 妬み嫉妬なんてない ('envidia, celos — esas cosas, no tenemos'); 好きになることなんて分からない ('eso de enamorarse, yo no lo entiendo'). Tono ligeramente desdeñoso.
explanation.pt-BR: なんて diminui ou afasta o que vem antes: 妬み嫉妬なんてない ('inveja, ciúme — coisas assim, não temos'); 好きになることなんて分からない ('essa coisa de se apaixonar, eu nem entendo'). Tom levemente dispensa.

name: Double-restriction 〜だけしか〜ない

explanation.en: Pattern stack: だけ ('only') + しか ('nothing but') + ない (negative). Two restrictive particles together for emphasis: 'I have ONLY X — and nothing else.' Stronger than だけ alone (which is neutral) or しか〜ない alone (which is negatively-framed). Ryuusei's 'だけしか信じられない' = 'I could only believe in that — and nothing else.' Common in self-deprecating reflections; not used in confident assertion.
explanation.es: Pila de partículas: だけ ('solo') + しか ('nada salvo') + ない (negativo). Dos partículas restrictivas juntas para énfasis: 'tengo SOLO X — y nada más'. Más fuerte que だけ solo (neutro) o しか〜ない solo (encuadrado negativo). El 'だけしか信じられない' de Ryuusei = 'solo podía creer en eso — nada más'. Común en autorreflexión; no en afirmación confiada.
explanation.pt-BR: Pilha de partículas: だけ ('só') + しか ('nada além de') + ない (negativo). Duas partículas restritivas juntas pra ênfase: 'tenho SÓ X — nada mais'. Mais forte que だけ sozinho (neutro) ou しか〜ない sozinho (enquadrado negativo). O 'だけしか信じられない' do Ryuusei = 'só conseguia acreditar nisso — nada mais'. Comum em autorreflexão; não usado em afirmação confiante.

name: Emphatic 〜だからこそ (precisely because)

explanation.en: Combination: だから ('because') + こそ ('precisely / exactly'). Adds emphasis to the causal relationship — not just 'because,' but 'PRECISELY because.' Hagane no Kokoro's '失くしたもの多いけれど だからこそ強くなれる' frames loss as the necessary precondition for strength: 'we lost a lot, BUT precisely because of that, we can become strong.' The pattern resists fatalism by embracing the cause.
explanation.es: Combinación: だから ('porque') + こそ ('precisamente'). Añade énfasis a la relación causal — no solo 'porque', sino 'JUSTAMENTE por eso'. El '失くしたもの多いけれど だからこそ強くなれる' de Hagane no Kokoro enmarca la pérdida como precondición necesaria de la fuerza: 'perdimos mucho, PERO justamente por eso podemos hacernos fuertes'. El patrón resiste el fatalismo abrazando la causa.
explanation.pt-BR: Combinação: だから ('porque') + こそ ('precisamente'). Adiciona ênfase à relação causal — não só 'porque', mas 'JUSTAMENTE por isso'. O '失くしたもの多いけれど だからこそ強くなれる' de Hagane no Kokoro enquadra a perda como pré-condição necessária da força: 'perdemos muito, MAS é justamente por isso que dá pra ficar forte'. O padrão resiste ao fatalismo abraçando a causa.

name: Emphatic 自分自身 (one's very self)

explanation.en: 自分 ('self') alone is the everyday reflexive. Adding 自身 ('one's self / one's body') doubles the reflexive for emphatic effect: 'I myself / you yourself.' Compare 私 → 私自身 ('I myself'), 君 → 君自身. The pattern stresses identity, especially when contrasting with others or with circumstances. Gurenge's 自分自身だけ ('only oneself') drives the point: the only person who can change you is YOU.
explanation.es: 自分 ('uno mismo') solo es el reflexivo cotidiano. Añadir 自身 ('el propio uno / el propio cuerpo') dobla el reflexivo para énfasis: 'yo mismo / tú mismo'. Compara 私 → 私自身, 君 → 君自身.
